title: Unpaid adult care changes the adaptation menu across employment positions
source_unit: 2024 SHED adult respondent grouped by regular unpaid adult care and employment status

observations.period: 2024; no regular unpaid adult care; not working

denominator.unit: published percentage base within care/employment group

observations.method: Weighted descriptive 2024 SHED cross-tab from the committed care/work analysis; each outcome uses its own nonmissing denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates; no design-based standard errors are reproduced and care/employment/adaptation fields have separate universes.
observations.subgroup: Adults not reporting regular unpaid adult care and not working.
observations.counterinterpretation: Nonworking status and lack of reported care do not imply low pressure or high choice; housing, health, debt, and other constraints remain unmeasured.

observations.period: 2024; no regular unpaid adult care; working part-time

denominator.unit: published percentage base within care/employment group

observations.method: Weighted descriptive 2024 SHED cross-tab from the committed care/work analysis; each outcome uses its own nonmissing denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates; no design-based standard errors are reproduced and care/employment/adaptation fields have separate universes.
observations.subgroup: Adults not reporting regular unpaid adult care and working part-time.
observations.counterinterpretation: Part-time work may be a chosen or constrained schedule; the table does not measure pay, hours, leave, control, or care substitution.

observations.period: 2024; no regular unpaid adult care; working full-time

denominator.unit: published percentage base within care/employment group

observations.method: Weighted descriptive 2024 SHED cross-tab from the committed care/work analysis; each outcome uses its own nonmissing denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates; no design-based standard errors are reproduced and care/employment/adaptation fields have separate universes.
observations.subgroup: Adults not reporting regular unpaid adult care and working full-time.
observations.counterinterpretation: Full-time employment coexists with borrowing and saving cuts; employment status is not a complete security or control measure.

observations.period: 2024; regular unpaid adult care; not working

denominator.unit: published percentage base within care/employment group

observations.method: Weighted descriptive 2024 SHED cross-tab from the committed care/work analysis; each outcome uses its own nonmissing denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates; no design-based standard errors are reproduced and care/employment/adaptation fields have separate universes.
observations.subgroup: Adults reporting regular unpaid adult care and not working.
observations.counterinterpretation: Caregivers can face substantial pressure without a paid-work response; this does not identify care hours, recipient need, or why they are not working.

observations.period: 2024; regular unpaid adult care; working part-time

denominator.unit: published percentage base within care/employment group

observations.method: Weighted descriptive 2024 SHED cross-tab from the committed care/work analysis; each outcome uses its own nonmissing denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates; no design-based standard errors are reproduced and care/employment/adaptation fields have separate universes.
observations.subgroup: Adults reporting regular unpaid adult care and working part-time.
observations.counterinterpretation: Part-time caregivers' reported pressure may reflect income, care intensity, or selection into part-time work; no causal care penalty is identified.

observations.period: 2024; regular unpaid adult care; working full-time

denominator.unit: published percentage base within care/employment group

observations.method: Weighted descriptive 2024 SHED cross-tab from the committed care/work analysis; each outcome uses its own nonmissing denominator.
observations.uncertainty: Self-reported cross-sectional estimates; no design-based standard errors are reproduced and care/employment/adaptation fields have separate universes.
observations.subgroup: Adults reporting regular unpaid adult care and working full-time.
observations.counterinterpretation: Full-time caregivers report higher borrowing and saving cuts than non-caregivers in this layer, but selection, income, health, and family support may explain the difference.

boundary: This is a weighted descriptive 2024 SHED comparison of regular unpaid adult care crossed with employment status. It does not measure care hours, recipient condition, pay, schedule control, paid replacement, or a causal effect of care on adaptation. The same respondent is not followed over time in this layer, and each outcome has its own nonmissing denominator.
